pages: An offer is a definite promise to be bound on specific terms.
An invitation to treat, such as goods displayed in a shop window, is not an offer.
Acceptance must be unconditional and match the offer exactly.
A counter-offer rejects the original offer.
Under the postal rule, acceptance is complete when the letter is posted.
Consideration is something of value given by each party.
Consideration must move from the promisee but need not be adequate.
In commercial agreements the intention is presumed.
In social and domestic agreements it is presumed not to exist.
